title: Reduced coordinates and group completion of the nodal monoid pushout
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative monoid, written additively, whose canonical map $P\to P^{\rm gp}$ is injective, with group completion as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $a\in P$. Set $R=\mathbf Z\oplus P$ and let $Q$ be the quotient of $\mathbf N^2\oplus R$ by the monoid congruence generated by $((1,1),0)\sim(0,(1,a))$. Write $u,v$ for the images of the two standard basis vectors of $\mathbf N^2$, $g:R\to Q$ for the canonical map and $e=g(1,0)$. Put $H=\mathbf Z\oplus\mathbf Z\oplus P^{\rm gp}$. The formula $h([(x,y,n,p)])=(x-y,n+y,p+ya)$ defines an injective monoid homomorphism $h:Q\to H$. Every class has a unique representative $(x,y,n,p)$ with $\min(x,y)=0$; for an arbitrary representative and $k=\min(x,y)$ this representative is $(x-k,y-k,n+k,p+ka)$. For $m\in\mathbf Z$ set $m_+=\max(m,0)$ and $m_-=\max(-m,0)$. The image of $h$ is precisely $\{(m,t,b)\in H:b-m_-a\in P\}$, where membership in $P$ means membership in its canonical image in $P^{\rm gp}$. For such $(m,t,b)$ the unique reduced representative is $(m_+,m_-,t-m_-,b-m_-a)$, its last coordinate interpreted as the unique preimage in $P$. The extension $h^{\rm gp}:Q^{\rm gp}\to H$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(m,t,b)\mapsto mu+te+g^{\rm gp}(0,b)$, where generators are read in $Q^{\rm gp}$ and $R^{\rm gp}$ is identified with $\mathbf Z\oplus P^{\rm gp}$. In these coordinates $u\mapsto(1,0,0)$, $v\mapsto(-1,1,a)$ and $g^{\rm gp}(n,b)\mapsto(0,n,b)$. No finite generation, saturation, sharpness or torsion-freeness of $P$ is assumed.

source.place: Historical ILO VI Proposition 1.9 input below lem-trf-local-term-locality: cocartesian monoid square defining Q and group calculation. Carries returned proof steps 1--2 and the coordinate group isomorphism in step 3. Agent-formulated explicit algebraic input to ILO VI Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71; the source omits these calculations. No Stacks tag states this nodal monoid calculation.

proof.text: On $A=\mathbf N^2\oplus\mathbf Z\oplus P$ define $F(x,y,n,p)=(x-y,n+y,[p]+y[a])$. Addition is componentwise, so $F(0)=0$ and $F(z+z')=F(z)+F(z')$. The two sides of the generating relation have the same image $(0,1,[a])$. Equality of $F$-images is a monoid congruence containing this relation, hence contains the congruence defining $Q$. Thus $F$ descends to a monoid homomorphism $h:Q\to H$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, cocartesian monoid square; elementary coordinate calculation supplied by Q52.

proof.text: If $x,y>0$, adding $(x-1,y-1,n,p)$ to the defining relation gives $(x,y,n,p)\sim(x-1,y-1,n+1,p+a)$. Induction on $k=\min(x,y)$, with the identity as base case $k=0$, therefore gives $(x,y,n,p)\sim(x-k,y-k,n+k,p+ka)$. In the induction step both first coordinates decrease by one, so their minimum decreases by one. The displayed representative belongs to $A$ and its first two coordinates have minimum zero.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, cocartesian monoid square; elementary coordinate calculation supplied by Q52.

proof.text: For a reduced representative put $m=x-y$. If $m\geq0$, reducedness gives $y=0,x=m$; if $m\leq0$, it gives $x=0,y=-m$. Thus always $x=m_+$ and $y=m_-$. Equality of $h$-images of two reduced representatives now gives equality of $x,y$, then of $n$ from $n+y$, and finally of $[p]$ from $[p]+y[a]$. Injectivity of $P\to P^{\rm gp}$ gives equality of $p$. Every class has a reduced representative by step 2, so this proves both its uniqueness and injectivity of $h$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, cocartesian monoid square; elementary coordinate calculation supplied by Q52.

proof.text: For a reduced representative with image $(m,t,b)$, step 3 gives $y=m_-$, whence $n=t-m_-$ and $[p]=b-m_-[a]$. Consequently every image satisfies $b-m_-[a]\in P$. Conversely, for a triple satisfying this condition let $p\in P$ be the unique preimage of $b-m_-[a]$, and take $(m_+,m_-,t-m_-,p)$. Its first two entries are natural numbers with minimum zero, its third entry is an arbitrary permitted integer, and substitution into $F$ gives $(m,t,b)$. This proves the stated image and inverse formula.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, cocartesian monoid square; elementary coordinate calculation supplied by Q52.

proof.text: Use the generators-and-relations definition of group completion in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], in additive notation. A homomorphism from a monoid $M$ to an abelian group $B$ extends by sending the generator $[z]$ of $M^{\rm gp}$ to its given image: the relation $[z+z']=[z]+[z']$ is respected. Two extensions agreeing on these generators are equal. In particular $R^{\rm gp}\simeq\mathbf Z\oplus P^{\rm gp}$: send $[(n,p)]$ to $(n,[p])$, and in the other direction send $(n,b)$ to $n[(1,0)]+\iota(b)$, where $\iota([p])=[(0,p)]$. These maps respect the displayed relations and are inverse on the generators $(n,p)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,[p])$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, cocartesian monoid square; elementary coordinate calculation supplied by Q52.

proof.text: Extend $h$ by the construction in step 5 to $h^{\rm gp}:Q^{\rm gp}\to H$, and similarly extend $g:R\to Q\to Q^{\rm gp}$ to $g^{\rm gp}$ using the identification of step 5. Define $j:H\to Q^{\rm gp}$ by $j(m,t,b)=mu+te+g^{\rm gp}(0,b)$; this is a group homomorphism by addition in the abelian group $Q^{\rm gp}$. Direct substitution gives $h^{\rm gp}(u)=(1,0,0)$, $h^{\rm gp}(v)=(-1,1,[a])$, $h^{\rm gp}(e)=(0,1,0)$ and $h^{\rm gp}g^{\rm gp}(n,b)=(0,n,b)$, the last equality first on $(1,0)$ and $(0,[p])$ and hence on their generated group. Thus $h^{\rm gp}j(m,t,b)=(m,t,b)$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, cocartesian monoid square; elementary coordinate calculation supplied by Q52.

proof.text: Conversely $jh^{\rm gp}$ fixes $u,e$ and every $g(0,p)$. For $v$ its value is $-u+e+g(0,a)=v$, since the relation in $Q$ is $u+v=e+g(0,a)$. Every element of $Q$ has the form $xu+yv+ne+g(0,p)$: this follows from a representative, and $g(n,0)=ne$ also for negative $n$ because $g$ is a homomorphism from $\mathbf Z\oplus P$. By the presentation in step 5 their images generate $Q^{\rm gp}$, so $jh^{\rm gp}$ is the identity on the whole group. Hence $j$ is the asserted inverse. All calculations used only the stated injectivity for $P$, never finite generation, saturation, sharpness or torsion-freeness.
